## Symptom

Run 44141097601 on main at 83ca81e709e: job `sweep (windows)` 134243804938 has 8 failures, all in `tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py`. Each fails with `AssertionError: pass_fds not supported on Windows.`, raised from `subprocess.Popen` in `FastImportSession.__init__` (`src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse_stream.py`). These are the only failures in that job, and they block `majestic-depilatory-beetle`, whose last acceptance criterion needs the job green.

The failing tests are `test_apply_collapses_below_horizon_history_and_preserves_reduced_state`, `test_cli_dry_run_reports_plan_without_updating_head`, `test_enforce_since_reanchor_makes_verify_authorship_clean`, `test_fast_import_preserves_metadata_timezone_and_raw_message_bytes`, `test_rewrites_snapshot_ledger_positions_to_new_checkpoint_sha`, `test_stream_failure_raises_and_leaves_the_branch_unchanged`, `test_streamed_engine_matches_the_rewrite_oracle` and `test_streamed_engine_runs_one_fast_import_and_one_batch_reader`.

## Cause

`FastImportSession` opens an `os.pipe()` and passes its write end to `git fast-import --cat-blob-fd=<fd>` through `pass_fds`, so it can read `get-mark` replies. CPython does not support `pass_fds` on Windows.

## Approach

git's documentation for `--cat-blob-fd` says responses to `get-mark`, `cat-blob` and `ls` go to stdout when the option is absent. The fix drops the extra pipe and `pass_fds`, starts fast-import with `stdout=subprocess.PIPE`, and reads each 40-hex `get-mark` reply from `proc.stdout`. With `--quiet` and no `progress` commands, nothing else is written to stdout. This uses no OS-specific feature, so no test is skipped or deselected on any platform.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse_stream.py`: read marks from stdout; drop the pipe and `pass_fds`.
- `tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py`: a regression test.

## Testing

- **Regression.** A test wraps `subprocess.Popen` in `reclaim_collapse_stream` so it raises `AssertionError("pass_fds not supported on Windows.")` whenever `pass_fds` is non-empty, as CPython does on Windows. It then runs a collapse that replays commits and asserts it succeeds. The test fails on the current code and passes with the fix.
- **Existing tests.** Every test in the module still passes, including the streamed-engine oracle and cost tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `FastImportSession` starts fast-import without `pass_fds` and reads `get-mark` replies from stdout. The new regression test fails before the change and passes after it.
- [x] Every test in `tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py` passes; `make verify` is run and any failure is fixed or shown environmental; the Gerrit change gets `Verified +1`.
- [x] After the merge, a `test.yml` run on main shows the `sweep (windows)` job passing; the run and job IDs are recorded on this ticket.
